Montalvo, by the way, is a freshman on the Central Connecticut State football team. Only four teams have done it twice. That group includes Killingly and Windsor in both 2024 and 2025, Naugatuck in 2023 and 2026, and Hand in 2024 and 2026. It shows just how tough it is to win football games. There were nine teams unbeaten following Week 9 last fall , and this season, there are eight, after Southington fell to New Britain 28-27 on Thursday, and Lyman Hall lost to Hand 35-14 on Friday. The undefeated teams left are Hand, Ludlowe, Masuk, Naugatuck, New London, North Branford and Plainville, all 8-0, and St. Joseph, which is 7-0. The Golden Hurricanes are 6-2, with their only losses coming against defending state champs Greenwich and New Canaan. No. 1 Ludlowe followed up its huge win at New Canaan with a 40-13 win over Trumbull . Naugatuck (8-0) got two rushing touchdowns and a touchdown pass from Qwentarvus Lee and won 41-12 over Seymour (5-3). Maloney (6-2) gave itself a massive boost in the Class L playoff hunt with a 55-40 win over Windsor (4-4). The Spartans have been averaging more than 40 points per game. Simsbury (7-1) defeated Newington 27-7 for its seventh win of the season. The Trojans had just four wins combined in the last three seasons. Cheshire (6-2) won its third straight game 35-10 over Sheehan (4-4) and is now in third place in the Class M standings. Darien (5-3) jumped into the top eight in Class L with a 34-14 win over Ridgefield (4-4). The Blue Wave will finish the regular season against Stamford and New Canaan. Up next Time has flown by. We are getting down to crunch time, as we amazingly get ready to enter Week 10 of the football season. There are a bushel of key games on deck, including a pair of matchups of ranked teams, when No. 1 Ludlowe faces No. 8 Staples in Westport on Friday at 7 p.m., and No. 2 St. Joseph hosts No. 4 Greenwich on Saturday at noon. item.description: Anthony Santander left many people in Toronto and the United States scratching their heads at his anti-Muslim social media posts. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) Getty Images On Tuesday night there was a blue wave in the United States. Apparently that didn’t sit right with a Blue Jay. By all accounts, Anthony Santander, the oft-injured and underperforming right fielder for the Toronto baseball club, was none-too-pleased with the results in Michigan’s Senate race. So he took to social media and posted the following: Anthony Santander thought it was a good idea to repost this anti-Muslim Instagram post. -Instagram He then posted another video that proclaimed that “Islam is not peaceful.” Luckily for Santander, the people of the United States and Canada have the freedom of speech, so nothing he said or posted was against the law. Luckily for the roughly four and half million Muslims in the United States and the nearly two million in Canada, they all have the freedom of religion. Santander is certainly not the first athlete to espouse his political (and/or religious) opinions in an open forum, and most certainly will not be the last. But he clearly recognized the error of his ways, as both posts were quickly deleted. The Blue Jays immediately distanced themselves from their right fielder, putting out a statement that read: “Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization’s values and beliefs.” Toronto signed Santander to a five year, $92.5 million contract prior to the 2025 season. Multiple shoulder injuries limited him to 54 games in his first year north of the border. He did go 3-for-16 in the 2025 post-season, but did not play after Game 3 of the American League Championship Series. The Blue Jays were able to win the pennant and come within the width of a spike of winning the World Series without his services, so maybe they don’t need him. That said, with Santander out for the entire season with a torn labrum, Toronto went 79-83 and came in in last place, so maybe they do. Santander still has three years and about $55 million left on his contract. Because what Santander posted is constitutionally protected and very difficult to categorize as “hate speech,” there is a real chance that he avoids punishment from either the club or the league. item.title: Josh Tongue ruled out of Australia ODIs with toe injury, England suffer fresh pace blow
item.description: England have suffered a setback ahead of their three-match ODI series against Australia, with fast bowler Josh Tongue ruled out due to a toe injury. The right-arm pacer will return to the United Kingdom for further assessment, leaving England without one of their promising fast-bowling options for the upcoming limited-overs assignment. Tongue, who was not included in England's plans for the five-match T20I series as he prepares for the team's upcoming Test tour of South Africa, has reportedly been carrying a problem with his left big toe since the recent tour of Pakistan. The injury also restricted his participation in the tri-series, where he featured in just one of England's four matches. Josh Tongue's injury concerns continue after Pakistan tour The 28-year-old's latest setback comes after an interrupted run in Pakistan, where the toe problem limited his involvement. He will now undergo further medical assessment in the UK to determine the extent of the injury and his recovery timeline. A regular feature of England's Test side over the past 12 months, Tongue has emerged as an important part of the country's fast-bowling plans. He made his ODI and T20I debuts earlier this year and has been viewed as one of England's promising pace options alongside Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker. England begin Australia tour with warm-up win England have already made a winning start to their tour of Australia, beating their opponents in a 50-over warm-up match in Perth on Saturday. The three-match ODI series is scheduled to begin next Friday, followed by a five-match T20I series. Tongue's absence will be a concern as England look to manage their fast-bowling resources across a demanding winter schedule. With the pacer not part of the limited-overs plans in the first place, the immediate focus will be on assessing his fitness ahead of the upcoming Test commitments. South Africa Test tour next on England's agenda England are scheduled to play a three-Test series in South Africa after their assignments in Australia. The team will have a warm-up match in Durban from December 9 to 11 before the opening Test gets underway in Johannesburg on December 17.

item.title: Arbeloa on King injury worry and Fulham’s draw with Newcastle
item.description: Arbeloa on King injury worry and Fulham’s draw with Newcastle Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa is hopeful Josh King has avoided a serious injury after the midfielder was forced off during the 1-1 draw with Newcastle United. King felt tightness in his groin with Fulham set to assess him further before determining the extent of the problem, and whether he can join up with England after receiving his first senior call up. “I think he felt a little bit tight on the groin,” Arbeloa said. “We will see, but I think it looks like nothing serious. item.title: Mics Catch Travis Kelce’s Powerful Message During Chiefs Game
item.description: Travis Kelce has established himself as one of the best tight ends in NFL history. He is in his 14th NFL season, all spent with the Kansas City Chiefs. The 37-year-old is still playing at a high level and also serves as a locker room leader. Mics caught him delivering a powerful message during a game. The Chiefs are coming off a loss to the Denver Broncos. It was their second consecutive defeat after starting the season 5-0. Patrick Mahomes had another strong performance, completing 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. Kelce recorded five catches for 87 yards. However, their efforts weren’t enough to avoid a 28-24 loss. Kansas City entered the season aiming to reclaim lost glory and prove that it is still Super Bowl contenders. The team missed the playoffs last year with a 6-11 record and Mahomes sustaining an ACL and LCL injury in December. Kelce, on the other hand, had a disappointing campaign by his standards. He finished with 76 receptions for 851 yards and five touchdowns. Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) on field against the Los Angeles Rams during the first half of the pre season at Arrowhead Stadium. Travis Kelce Sends Strong Message to Servicemen The Chiefs posted a video of Kelce on Instagram on Friday. He sent a strong message to troops in attendance. It came two days ahead of their Salute To Service Week 9 matchup with the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium. “Thank you for your service guys,” Kelce said. “Much love, baby. How about it, Bearcat love there.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kansas City Chiefs (@chiefs) The former Cincinnati Bearcats star has a chance to produce a vintage performance on Sunday. Kelce has had decent games but has shown throughout his career that he is capable of producing even better numbers. Kansas City is desperate to get back to its winning ways, and the presence of servicemen inside the venue could motivate the team to win. Salute To Service is in its 16th year. It recognizes the efforts of NFL players, coaches and staffs’ efforts in empowering military personnel and families. The Chiefs nominated team legend Kendall Gammon to win the award this year. Kentucky’s average of 3.55 yards per carry allowed does not explain THAT level of ineptitude. The inability to scheme up anything remotely near a useful rushing attack is brutal. The kicking specialists had another very good game. Brock Taylor went 1 for 1 from 30 yards out. Easy work for him. Ebel’s stat line of 3 punts for 119 yards looks pretty rough, but that was not always about him. The first punt was a 26-yard kick that was caught by Davin Chandler at the 15 instead of letting it bounce to potentially pin Kentucky even deeper. The second punt was a 60-yard effort that was returned 12 yards for a 48-yard net. The final one was a 33-yard punt that I frankly do not remember and did not even mark down in the re-watch notes. Still, it was maybe one sub-par kick from Ebel. To be clear, for all my comments about Jared Curtis’s turnovers, he was stellar for 90% of the game. Another TD was scored on just 47 yards after the interception. One FG was scored after 4 yards off the fumble. Another 3 came after 46 yards. They just needed to be a bit more buttoned up. The TDs were all 10 yard plays or shorter. Two were from the 1. They never broke, but they bent just a bit too much. The offense did use more misdirection, especially in the first half. They were using motion and fakes consistently thoughout the game, but I think the first two drives were 80 or 90 percent usage. It was not the same offense as Pavia, as evidenced by the pass-heavy balance. The “identity” was there early Saturday then they backed off a bit. The Commodores jumped to a 10-0 lead by forcing 2 straight 3-and-outs. The players fought throughout. There was no fear. There were mistakes. The coaches have to keep the pressure and fire up. Do not worry about “safe.” Worry about stepping on the opponents’ throats. Missed opportunities continue to plague this team almost as badly as penalties. There were two dropped picks. One of the drives allowd to continue ended in a TD. The other was allowed to flip field position. Vanderbilt’s second offensive drive only scored a FG after starting at the Kentucky 20. None of the plays alone would have made a 17-point difference, but they could have changed situations and pressure, potentially mitigating other mistakes. Snowball effect and whatnot. Lessons for Further Study Can this team build some momentum for the offseason? Barring a 2016/2018 type run to the finish, postseason football is dead. They do need to have success down the stretch if they want to make big transfer portal moves. And avoid losing their own players to the highest bidder.

item.title: This PGA Tour pro went full ‘Etch-A-Sketch’ with a 12 at Tiger’s course
item.description: LOS CABOS – Christo Lamprecht made a Tom Brady at the 460-yard par-4 15th hole at El Cardonal at Diamante on Saturday. No, this doesn’t have anything to do with Brady’s incredible seven Super Bowl titles but rather the retired New England Patriots quarterback great’s uniform number. The lanky South African carded a 12 at the Tiger Woods-designed layout during the third round of the PGA Tour's 2026 World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos, Mexico. The dogleg-left hole plays uphill, with bunkers framing the left side of the tee shot. A deceptive wide landing area lies beyond the bunkers. Lamprecht ripped his tee shot left of left, or as ShotLink termed it, “to unknown,” and he had to re-tee and take a penalty. He kept his third shot on the planet but tugged this one into the left native area. He hacked out into a fairway bunker and that’s when the adventure really began. His shot tracking on PGA Tour.com looks like a kid drawing on an Etch-a-Sketch and included multiple shots of ping-pong back and forth before he finally found the putting surface with his 10th shot. The green’s distinct undulations adds to the complexity of the hole and Lamprecht got the full Tiger treatment at 15. Lamprecht missed the 34-foot putt and tapped in from 19 inches. But not before having to scratch two numbers in the box at 15 for a dozen. Suffice it to say, Lamprecht, who made the cut by a shot after rounds of 70-68, plummeted to last in the field as he moved in the wrong direction on Moving Day. Adam Schupak is a senior writer for Golfweek, covering the PGA Tour. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: This PGA Tour pro went full ‘Etch-A-Sketch’ with a 12 at Tiger’s course

item.description: PORTLAND, OREGON - OCTOBER 29: Ja Morant #1 of the Portland Trail Blazers looks on against the Memphis Grizzlies at Moda Center on October 29, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Ja Morant had two replies for Vit Krejci after his Portland Trail Blazers teammate fractured his left ankle. The first was a word of encouragement. The second made clear Krejci had company. “Hold yo head , we’ll never fall,” Morant wrote in one Instagram comment, adding a prayer-hands emoji. In another, he wrote, “we with you brudda.” Krejci had used the post to talk about patience and what he had learned from previous setbacks. “I’ve faced adversity many times before, and every setback has taught me something valuable,” he wrote. He closed by thanking people who had reached out. Trae Young, Krejci’s former Atlanta Hawks teammate, chimed in with “Get right brotha!” and a heart emoji. View this post on Instagram Ja Morant and Vit Krejci Are Both Sidelined for Portland Krejci was hurt late in the third quarter of Portland’s 132-119 win over the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He went down after trying to draw a charge on Miles Bridges and finished with five points, three rebounds and two assists in 12 minutes. Coach Micah Nori disclosed the fracture after the game. The NBA’s Friday injury report listed it as a left ankle fracture. Morant is working through his own recovery. The Blazers announced Oct. 30 that he had a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and would be re-evaluated in four weeks . Portland had ruled out both players for Friday’s game against the Lakers , along with Shaedon Sharpe, who is recovering from right meniscus surgery. Krejci’s Instagram post focused on his mindset and gave no return date. Blazers Turn to Sidy Cissoko and Chris Youngblood The first look at Portland’s bench without Krejci came Friday in a 124-118 NBA Cup loss to the Lakers. Sidy Cissoko played 22 minutes and Chris Youngblood played nearly 11 . They scored seven points apiece and combined to make four 3-pointers on nine attempts. That shooting is one part of what Portland needs to replace. Krejci averaged 7.2 points in about 19 minutes per game for the Blazers after they acquired him from Atlanta in February. item.title: Pundit says this win shows how far Arsenal have come
item.description: Pundit says this win shows how far Arsenal have come Arsenal continued their impressive Premier League campaign with a 1-0 victory over Hull City , but Paul Robinson believes the Gunners may have struggled to secure such a result in previous seasons. Mikel Arteta’s side controlled much of the contest and had opportunities to win by a more convincing margin, yet they ultimately had to settle for a narrow victory. Despite the scoreline, the result demonstrated another important aspect of Arsenal’s development. They have become more capable of handling difficult matches and finding ways to collect three points, even when their performances do not produce the number of goals their dominance might suggest. In the past, Arsenal could have allowed frustration to affect their approach in games like this. However, the current team appears better equipped to deal with opponents who make life difficult, showing the resilience needed to maintain a challenge for major honours. Arsenal have developed a winning mentality The Gunners will recognise that they could have made the afternoon more comfortable by converting more of their opportunities. Nevertheless, winning remains the priority, and another three points will matter far more than the margin of victory as they continue their campaign. Robinson has followed the club’s progress and believes the difference between the current side and previous Arsenal teams is clear. The former goalkeeper has seen the difficulties they experienced in earlier seasons and recognises the improvements that have helped them become more consistent. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Robinson praises Arsenal’s resilience Speaking on Premier League Productions , Robinson highlighted how much the team have improved and why their latest result reflects that progress. “I don’t think Arsenal win that game two seasons ago – that shows how far they’ve come in a short space of time. They’ve got real resilience now. They’re a team of winners. They find a way to win, week after week, and they’re setting the standards.” Arteta will want his players to keep improving, particularly in front of goal, but the result offers another reason for satisfaction. Arsenal are finding ways to win matches that might previously have caused them problems, and that quality could prove valuable as the season progresses. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Falcons vs. Bengals series history: Win-loss record, matchup results
item.description: 24 Nov 1996: Running back Jamal Anderson #32 of the Atlanta Falcons carries the football during the Falcons 41-31 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at Riverfront Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mandatory Credit: Jed Jacobsohn /Allsport | Getty Images The Falcons head back into play against the AFC this week, and they do so across the pond in the second ever NFL game to be played in the Spanish capital of Madrid, at the esteemed Estadio de Santiago Bernebéu. Their opponent in that game will be the Cincinnati Bengals, who have won two games out of every three against the Birds, owning a very aesthetically pleasing 10-5 all time record against Atlanta. The majority of that damage came before the turn of the millennia, with the Bengals winning seven out of 10 matchups against the overmatched Falcons through the 1996 season, with games between these teams happening on averaged every three years in that time period. The Birds pulled back a little bit with three consecutive victories — in 2002, 2006 and 2010 — to pull the series close to even. That was quickly followed with three straight Bengals victories which brings us to where we are today, with two of those coming in the Matt Ryan era, which was also the most successful one in Falcons history. The Bengals caught Atlanta in a down year of that era twice in a row, in 2014 and 2018. When these teams met last The Falcons had some confidence about them in year 2 of the Arthur Smith regime, having just pulled back to .500 at 3-3, with a victory against the 49ers after some questionable reffing cost them against Tampa the week before. The Bengals sported the same record, but they proved from the start that they were on another level. It took exactly two minutes for second year man Joe Burrow to hit Tyler Boyd on a 60-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Then after a Falcon punt, the Bengals punched the ball in again following a longer drive. Then an Atlanta three and out was followed with a Burrow to rookie Ja’Marr Chase touchdown on the first play of the second quarter, before the two connected in the end zone again on the back end of the same quarter. By halftime the game was effectively over as the Falcon offense spent the second half completely one dimensional and getting terrorized by the Bengal defense, with Burrow putting the finishing touches on with a rushing score to complete his magnificent day. Up 35-17, one of the most impressive feats by the Bengal offense was getting the ball back via punt at their own 3-yard-line (why the Falcons punted it near midfield down three scores in the fourth quarter I don’t know) with 8:44 left in the game and choking away that entire clock (and all three Atlanta timeouts) with a 17-play drive which went 95 yards and ended in a kneel down.

item.title: Leandro Trossard makes bold Celtic claim after dramatic Besiktas defeat
item.description: Leandro Trossard makes bold Celtic claim after dramatic Besiktas defeat Besiktas winger Leandro Trossard believes his side were the better team against Celtic despite suffering a dramatic 3-2 Europa League defeat at Parkhead on Thursday night. The Belgian international, who featured for Arsenal in June’s Champions League final, insisted the Turkish outfit controlled much of the encounter but were ultimately punished for costly defensive mistakes. Martin O’Neill’s side overturned a first-half deficit following the introduction of several substitutes, with Camilo Durán netting a dramatic winner after Besiktas had briefly restored parity. Besiktas boss Vincenzo Italiano had already claimed his side ‘gifted’ Celtic all three goals, and Trossard echoed those frustrations while insisting the visitors deserved something from the contest. Speaking to TNT Sports, Trossard said: “I think we controlled the first-half especially. We were the better team, and then we made a mistake. “In the second half, we gave the goals away too easily, and then it was a bit of chaos for us. So we need to be better than that, because I think in general we played better than them, but we need to take our chances as well. Asked whether Besiktas had been drawn into Celtic’s style of play, he continued: “Maybe, yeah, but I think lately it’s been too many times for us where we are not sharp enough on the counter attacks and stuff like that. “And then, at this level you get punished, and then exactly today that’s what happened again. It’s learning, for sure, but we can’t repeat this every week. So we need to act now. There’s a game coming up on Sunday again, so we need to be ready for that.” Reflecting on Besiktas’ strong start to the Europa League campaign, Trossard admitted the defeat was particularly frustrating given his side’s performance. He added: “That’s why as well, we wanted to continue our form in this competition. It’s a shame that we didn’t take at least one point today, because I think we deserved it, but that’s what football’s about. Now we need to keep our heads up and move onto the next one.” Asked whether Besiktas could recover from the setback, he concluded: “Yeah, for sure. item.title: Taylor Fritz handed bad news after losing to Carlos Alcaraz in Paris as Stockholm draw is announced
item.description: Taylor Fritz will be left with a strong feeling of what could have been after his brutal defeat to Carlos Alcaraz at the Paris Masters. Fritz was beaten by Alcaraz in an epic encounter in the French capital, which ended 6-7(10-12), 7-5, 6-3 in favour of the Spaniard. Worryingly for the American, he had two match points in their lengthy Paris Masters battle. But Alcaraz produced a stunning comeback to secure the win and a semifinal clash with Casper Ruud. Meanwhile, Fritz will be desperate to bounce back from his French nightmare at the Stockholm Open , but that won’t be easy given his projected draw in Sweden. Taylor Fritz handed tricky Stockholm draw after Carlos Alcaraz loss Fritz is the top seed at the ATP 250 tournament, which immediately follows the Paris Masters in the calendar. And that seeding means he has received a first round bye, which is welcome news for the American following his efforts against Alcaraz. After that, however, he faces a tricky opening test against either Cameron Norrie or James Duckworth. And in the quarterfinals, he could be tasked with taking on one of Holger Rune, Arthur Rinderknech or Zizou Bergs. Lorenzo Musetti then represents a possible semifinal opponent for Fritz, who could meet Ruud in the final of the Stockholm Open. The Norwegian is the defending champion at the tournament, having won last year’s final against Ugo Humbert, who incidentally is also a potential semifinal opponent for Fritz. It’s certainly not an easy possible route to the title, which would represent a second ATP success for the American in 2026, and the 12th of his career. Ben Shelton ends five-year Taylor Fritz run in ATP rankings Aside from his collapse against Alcaraz, Fritz has added motivation to emerge victorious in Sweden. His defeat has had a major impact on the ATP Finals, for which the American has now failed to qualify. He was in the running to secure the final place for Turin later this month, but his Paris Masters exit has put an end to that contention. Instead, Alcaraz’s win has ensured that his fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar has claimed the last spot. And his qualification represents history for the sport, with Jodar becoming the first player to reach the ATP Finals in the same year he made his tour-level debut. The achievement comes shortly after Jodar broke into the ATP top 10 in record time. Meanwhile, Fritz’s ranking is also of significance. He will now finish 2026 behind Ben Shelton, who will be America’s year-end number one. That brings an end to a fine run from Fritz, who held that honour every year since 2021.

But one way that it was absolutely better was that in Game 1, the Heels were outrebounded by 9, which gave Western a bunch of extra chances that they took just enough advantage of to keep the game uncomfortably close. Against Wofford, the Heels were +7, which isn’t domination by any means but is enough to keep an otherwise outplayed opponent from changing the game. And almost inarguably the biggest reason for that, and thus the reason that the Heels were able to play like the clearly superior team, was Maximo Adams, who absolutely hoovered the ball off the glass in his team-leading 22 minutes. item.description: Everton Interest In Brazilian Striker Confirmed: Is A £43m Fee Wise? David Moyes has spent the autumn proving that this summer’s upheaval left Everton stronger than anyone expected. A 3-1 comeback win over Coventry City at the Hill Dickinson Stadium lifted the Toffees to fifth in the Premier League, and the result came in Moyes’ 592nd game in charge, which equalled Harry Catterick’s club record. A Carabao Cup quarter-final against Fleetwood Town also awaits. Little of that looked likely in the summer. item.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
item.description: As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season. Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A footballing alien’: Mamadou Sangaré soars to Premier League heights
item.description: Brentford’s Mali midfielder stood out when he was six and has shone in the Premier League since £39m transfer “When I first saw him, I thought to myself: ‘Who on earth is this player?’ laughs Youness Bengelloun as he remembers Mamadou Sangaré. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
